title: Geostationary Satellite
notes: **Definition:** a satellite that appears fixed over one point on the equator, orbiting Earth in the equatorial plane from west to east with period exactly 24 hours.
**Three conditions:** (1) orbit in the equatorial plane, (2) period $T = 24$ hours, (3) direction west to east (same as Earth's rotation).
**Orbital radius:** $r = \sqrt[3]{\frac{GM T^2}{4\pi^2}} \approx 42,400\,\text{km}$ from Earth's centre, or altitude $\approx 35,800\,\text{km}$ above the surface.
**Why geostationary is useful:** a single satellite at this altitude can monitor weather, relay communications, or broadcast TV over one-third of Earth's surface.
**Limitation:** only satellites directly above the equator can be geostationary. Satellites at other inclinations cannot remain fixed over one point.
